meta.title: URL Abuse × Lookyloo
meta.description: Planned architecture: URL Abuse is the single orchestrator (rebuilt backend, API and data stream kept), Lookyloo is one provider called through PyLookyloo, other providers come later. Arrows show the calls and the data flows.

nodes.label:
Analysts
(browser)
nodes.description: People who check a suspicious link through the URL Abuse web interface.

nodes.label:
Existing integrations
(scripts, feeds, partners)
nodes.description: Tools that already push URLs to URL Abuse and read its results. They keep working: the API and the incoming data stream keep their format.

nodes.label: URL Abuse
nodes.description: URL Abuse (CIRCL): the single place where a URL is checked. Its backend is rebuilt; it orchestrates the providers and aggregates their results.

nodes.label:
Web view
(new interface)
nodes.description: The new URL Abuse interface: per-check progress and a clear verdict.

nodes.label:
Public API
(kept, same format)
nodes.description: The URL Abuse API is maintained so that existing clients keep working.

nodes.label:
Backend (rebuilt)
orchestrates providers,
aggregates the results
nodes.description: Almost nothing exists in the current URL Abuse backend: it is rewritten. It calls each provider through its own client library and builds one report per URL.

nodes.label: Lookyloo
nodes.description: Lookyloo is one provider among others: captures the URL in a real browser (redirects, resources, screenshot, tree, indexes). Nothing URL Abuse specific is added to Lookyloo.

nodes.label:
MISP modules
(later)
nodes.description: Planned provider: expansion and enrichment modules of MISP.

nodes.label:
Other services
(DNS, WHOIS, reputation...)
(later)
nodes.description: Planned providers: a URL is a pivot towards many services; each one is plugged into the URL Abuse backend the same way.

nodes.label:
Decisions

• One implementation: the logic lives in URL Abuse, not duplicated in Lookyloo.
• Lookyloo stays a provider like any other, called with PyLookyloo (which has all the calls); no URL Abuse view or logic inside Lookyloo.
• The URL Abuse API and the incoming data stream are kept for compatibility.
• Other providers (MISP modules, pivot services) are added later in the same way.
nodes.description: What was agreed for the URL Abuse / Lookyloo integration.
